monthly_review.summary: This month shows increased volume and intensity versus last month, with faster average pace and higher time in Z3–Z4, but cadence dropped slightly and efficiency worsened — suggesting fatigue or compromised form under load.
monthly_review.highlight: Pace improved significantly (-37 sec/km) while efficiency worsened (+0.46 ml/kg/km) and aerobic TE rose — a classic signature of accumulated fatigue rather than fitness gain, confirmed by the sharp drop in cadence and rising Z3–Z4 share (33% this month vs 26% last).

goal_tracker.message: The runner has already exceeded last month’s volume by 27.2 km and 5 sessions — no further running is needed to 'match' last month. Given compromised readiness and worsening efficiency/TE, chasing additional volume in the final day would increase fatigue without benefit.

insights.title: Pace–efficiency decoupling
insights.body: Average pace improved by 37 sec/km (497 → 534 sec/km) while running economy worsened from 14.12 to 14.58 ml/kg/km — indicating pace gains are coming at a metabolic cost, not improved efficiency.

insights.title: Z3–Z4 dominance displacing Z1–Z2 recovery work
insights.body: Z1 dropped from 43% (Aug) to 18% (Sep), while Z3+Z4 rose from 34% to 53% — a 19-point shift toward moderate-to-hard effort without compensatory low-intensity volume to support recovery or aerobic base development.

insights.title: Cadence–stride length trade-off under fatigue
insights.body: Cadence fell from 149 spm (Aug) to 146 spm (Sep) while stride length increased (inferred from recent runs: 76.4 → 86.5 m at fastest efforts), suggesting compensation for fatigue that may elevate injury risk over time.
